reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification of every numbered line.
0001: Framing sentence ('I am trying to prove the following statement'), no mathematical content; nothing to justify.
0002: Blank line; vacuous.
0003: States the claim to be proved: lim_{n->inf} f(n)/g(n) = infinity implies f = Omega(g) and f != O(g). Acceptable as the goal statement; note it implicitly presupposes g(n) != 0 (and, for the standard asymptotic definitions, g(n) > 0 eventually), an assumption never made explicit.
0004: Blank; vacuous.
0005: Horizontal rule / formatting; vacuous.
0006: Section heading 'What I've done so far'; no content.
0007-0008: Formatting rules; vacuous.
0009: Unfolds the hypothesis as 'for all M > 0 there exists n_0 such that for all n >= n_0, f(n)/g(n) > M'. This is the correct definition of divergence to +infinity of the quotient, so the step is justified (modulo the unstated fact that the quotient is defined, i.e. g(n) != 0 for large n).
0010: Multiplies the inequality f(n)/g(n) > M by g(n) to get f(n) > M*g(n). Justified only if g(n) > 0 for all n >= n_0; if g(n) < 0 the inequality reverses. Positivity of g is standard in this asymptotic context but is nowhere stated or derived, so the step is justified only under an unstated hypothesis — a gap, though a benign one.
0011: FIRST FAILING STEP. The author picks c_1 satisfying '0 <= M <= c_1' and asserts this yields 0 <= c_1*g(n) <= f(n). The inequality is used in the wrong direction: from f(n) > M*g(n) and g(n) > 0, c_1 >= M gives c_1*g(n) >= M*g(n), which does NOT imply c_1*g(n) <= f(n). The correct choice is 0 < c_1 <= M (e.g. fix M = 1 and take c_1 = 1), which yields c_1*g(n) <= M*g(n) < f(n). Additionally the step needs the quantifier structure spelled out (the Omega definition requires exhibiting one constant c_1 > 0 and one threshold n_0, obtained by instantiating the limit definition at a particular M), and c_1 must be strictly positive, not merely >= 0, since c_1 = 0 makes the Omega bound trivial and useless. As written the chain of inequalities does not follow.
0012: Concludes f(n) = Omega(g(n)). The conclusion is true under the hypothesis, but it is not established here because it rests on the invalid inequality manipulation of 0011.
0013: Blank; vacuous.
0014: Formatting rule; vacuous.
0015: 'So now my questions are:' — meta-commentary, no proof content.
0016: Asks whether the first part is correct; this is a question, not a justified step, and it confirms the argument is not being asserted as complete.
0017: Asks how to prove f(n) != O(g(n)); the second half of the required claim is therefore never proved. No step anywhere in the text establishes it, so even if 0011 were repaired the argument would remain incomplete with respect to the problem statement.
0018: Blank; vacuous.
0019: States the author is struggling with the second part; no content.
0020: Sketches an unexecuted plan (reductio: assume f = O(g) with constant c_2 and derive a contradiction) and explicitly disclaims confidence in it. A plan is not a proof; the contradiction (instantiate the limit at M = c_2 to get f(n) > c_2*g(n) for large n, contradicting f(n) <= c_2*g(n)) is never carried out.
0021-0022: Closing thanks; vacuous.
Overall: the target statement is true under the standard positivity assumptions, but this text is a question post rather than a proof. The Omega half contains a genuine reversed-inequality error at line 0011 (c_1 must satisfy 0 < c_1 <= M, not M <= c_1), and the not-O half is not proved at all, only wished for. Verdict INVALID, first failure at 0011.
